text: To go and tell any friend, wife, or mistress, any secret with which they have nothing to do, is discovering to them such an unretentive weakness, as must convince them that you will tell it to twenty others, and consequently that they may reveal it without the risk of being discovered.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter L, to his son, London, September 13, Old Style 1748
